Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase. Kate Pelle and Ines McKeon walks out as the openers for Australia Women Under-19. Rashmika Sewwandi to bowl. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Australia Women Under-19 bowled and fielded brilliantly after the first 6 overs. Lily Bassingthwaighte for her 3 for 31, and Hasrat Gill with her 2 wickets gave them the breakthrough they needed to get better of Sumudu Nisansala. Now Australia Women Under-19 face a challenge of 100 runs in 20 overs with a good Sri Lanka Women Under-19 spin attack infront of them. It is going to be a very good chase from the viewers' perspective. Will Australia take the game easily? Or will the spin attack of Sri Lanka Women Under-19 have all the right answers? Let's find out in the run chase coming up.

Sri Lanka Women Under-19 managed 99 runs in 20 overs after losing 8 wickets after being 41 without loss after the first 6! Australia Women Under-19 turned the game on its head and the credit goes to Lily Bassingthwaighte and Hasrat Gill for the 5 wickets between them. Sri Lanka Women Under-19 started brilliantly with the bat with both openers looking in good touch. Both Sumudu Nisansala and Sanjana Kavindi managed a 46-run partnership for the first wicket in less than 8 overs. After the fall of both the openers, Australia Women Under-19 kept a tight grip on the scoring with their fielding and bowling changes. Some brilliant catches in the deep from the Australia Women Under-19 team and Sri Lanka Women Under-19 were kept quiet throughout the innings.

The match officials and the players of both teams walk out to the ground in lines for the National Anthems. It is the national anthem of Sri Lanka first, followed by that of Australia.

Lucy Hamilton, the captain of Australia Women Under-19 says that they were looking to bowl first and she is happy with the toss. She further adds that they have a deep batting line up and the girls are ready for the chase. They will want to contain the batters as early as possible.

Manudi Nanayakkara the skipper of Sri Lanka Women Under-19 says that they want to bat first and continues by saying that they have had some good games and will look to continue the same today. She adds that they want a good start to the batting, especially in the first 6 overs. She ends by saying that they are playing with the same team.

With the semifinalists already locked in, Match 12, the last game of the Super Six stage in the ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup, 2025, sees unbeaten Australia Women Under-19 take on Sri Lanka Women Under-19 at the YSD-UKM Cricket Oval in Bangi. This match is a chance for both teams to showcase their strengths, Australia Women Under-19 to maintain their invincible streak heading into the semis and Sri Lanka to bow out of the tournament on a high. Australia have been a dominant force throughout the competition, demonstrating clinical all-round performances in nearly every game. Despite a few hiccups with the top order early in the tournament, their dependable middle order, led by skipper Lucy Hamilton, has consistently risen to the challenge. What makes this Aussie side formidable is their depth, with different players stepping up at critical junctures, ensuring they’re never overly reliant on just one or two individuals. On the bowling front, their disciplined attack has been crucial, consistently breaking partnerships and keeping opposition batters under pressure. Sri Lanka Women Under-19, meanwhile, come into this game after a washed-out fixture against Scotland that dashed their semifinal hopes. While they’ve shown flashes of brilliance throughout the tournament, they’ve lacked the finishing touch needed to cross the line in key moments. Opener Sanjana Kavindi has been a standout performer, combining with Manudi Nanayakkara and Dahami Sanethma to provide the bulk of their runs. However, the bowling department, led by Chamudi Praboda, has been less consistent, with the inability to contain runs proving costly at critical stages. This game offers Sri Lanka Women Under-19 a golden opportunity to play fearlessly, with no pressure on qualification, and test themselves against the best in the tournament. For Australia Women Under-19, it’s another chance to fine-tune their already impressive machine before heading into the semifinals. With their sights set on the trophy, Australia will aim for a clinical finish, but Sri Lanka has the potential to spring a surprise. Can Sri Lanka break the Aussies' winning streak, or will Australia continue their dominant march toward the title? We shall soon find out!
